title: Iterating to a Pose: Damped Least Squares for Any Arm, Why It Needs the Damping, and What It Finds Instead of Eight

questions.question: What does damping do to the step near a singularity?
options: Makes the iteration take fewer steps everywhere
Limits it, at a little cost in accuracy
questions.explanation: Adding lambda squared to the diagonal keeps the inverse from blowing up. The step is a little less accurate in the easy directions and bounded in the hard one.

questions.question: Near a straight elbow the plain step and the damped step were:
questions.explanation: With the elbow 0.002 rad from straight a centimetre of error asked for more than three turns. Damped, the same error asked for 0.021 rad.

questions.question: From a start of all zeros the UR5 converged in how many of 40 poses?
questions.explanation: It only improves the error locally, and from far away it can stop where no small step helps. From starts near the answer it reached 37.

questions.question: What did a pose out of reach do?
options: Stopped at the limit of steps, 0.64 m away, with ok false
Returned the nearest pose with ok true
Stopped at once with zero steps
questions.explanation: The error cannot reach zero, so the step limit ends it and the result says it did not converge.

questions.question: Why did the Panda's solutions differ from the joint angles that made the pose?
options: It has seven joints: a family of angles reaches the same pose
questions.explanation: Seven joints for six numbers of pose leaves one freedom over. The iteration lands on whichever member of the family is near its start.

questions.question: On the typical arm which of the eight did the iteration find?
options: The one with the elbow up, every time
One of them, depending on the start: 29 of 40 were among the eight
None: iteration finds poses the closed form misses
questions.explanation: A local method ends at a solution near where it began. 29 of 40 were among the eight; the rest did not converge.
